content.value_statement: Writing correct SQL across database dialects is slow and error-prone. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create safe DBX Studio queries.
actual_capabilities: Generates dialect-aware SQL for PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, MySQL, and SQLite.
Uses schema inspection before writing queries when DBX Studio tools are available.
Builds SELECT queries with limits, CTEs, aggregations, and window functions.
Helps debug SQL by checking table names, column names, and query structure.
Explains query results in clear business language after tool execution.
limitations: It is designed for DBX Studio workflows and may rely on DBX Studio AI tools.
It focuses on read-only SELECT and WITH queries, not data modification commands.
It cannot verify live schema or row data unless connected tools provide that context.
It does not replace database permissions, access controls, or human review.

use_cases.title: Explore Customer Data
use_cases.description: Create limited SELECT queries that inspect customer records, trends, and segments in DBX Studio.

use_cases.title: Debug Query Results
use_cases.description: Check SQL structure, column names, joins, and filters when a query returns unexpected results.

use_cases.title: Build Reporting Metrics
use_cases.description: Generate CTEs, aggregations, and window functions for revenue, activity, and operational dashboards.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Basic Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a safe table preview.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use DBX Studio schema tools to write a limited SELECT query for the table I name. Explain the result in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Recent Activity
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dialect-aware query that summarizes recent activity by date and category. Validate table and column names first.

prompt_templates.title: Debug an Existing Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my SQL query for errors, missing columns, unsafe assumptions, and dialect issues. Suggest a corrected read-only version.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Analytics Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a CTE-based analytics query with ranking, aggregation, and clear result interpretation. Use limits unless I request all rows.

output_examples.input: Show revenue by month for the last year.
output_examples.output: The skill validates the date and amount columns, groups revenue by month, limits output, and reports the latest monthly totals clearly.
The skill uses a ranking approach, returns one recent order per user, and explains which ordering column controls the result.

output_examples.input: Why is my query failing in BigQuery?
output_examples.output: The skill checks dialect rules, identifier quoting, and missing columns, then suggests a corrected read-only query structure.

best_practices: Ask for the database dialect and business goal before writing complex SQL.
Validate tables and columns with schema tools before executing a query.
Use limits and read-only queries unless a trusted workflow explicitly allows more.
anti_patterns: Do not guess table names when schema tools are available.
Do not run broad queries without limits on large production tables.
Do not use this skill for migrations, destructive commands, or permission changes.

faq.question: Which database dialects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, MySQL, and SQLite patterns.

faq.question: Can it run SQL queries?
faq.answer: It can guide DBX Studio AI tool use for read-only SELECT and WITH queries when those tools are available.

faq.question: Does it modify database data?
faq.answer: No. The skill is written for read-only query generation and analysis.

faq.question: Can it optimize slow queries?
faq.answer: It can suggest clearer filters, joins, aggregations, and dialect-aware patterns based on provided schema context.

faq.question: Does it require DBX Studio?
faq.answer: The guidance is tailored to DBX Studio and its AI database tools.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive data?
faq.answer: Use normal database permissions and review outputs. The skill does not replace access controls or privacy policy requirements.
